what: Two-sided bounds on the least dissipation g(3/10, 2/25) of a hidden finite-state network whose binary lamp, read at Poisson times of rate 2, has C1 = 3/10 and C2 = 2/25: networks decided as upper bounds, and the finite conditions of a lower-bound certificate, with the controls that must be refused.
saysFirst: The question and the phenomenon are Dobrynin and Stroujkova's (arXiv:2611.24898, 18 November 2026): a time-reversible binary record that still requires dissipation, and the least dissipation over all finite networks left open. This record decides a two-sided bound on one constant of a snapshot version of it. The upper bound is decided: a network that reproduces the two numbers exactly. The lower bound is a certificate whose finite conditions are decided here; the two theorems that turn it into a bound were proved by one AI model and read once by the other, and are not decided.

lower.reading_of_format: functions = [A_0..A_{na-1}, K_0..K_{nk-1}, P_0..P_{npsi-1}], each the values at the knots 0 = h_0 < ... < h_K = 1, linear in |h| between knots; A and P odd in h (A(h) = sign(h) A(|h|)), K even (K(h) = K(|h|)); p = sum A_k d^(2k), q = sum K_k d^(2k+1), psi = sum P_k d^(2k+1); w = h + d, v = h - d, beta = p + q, gamma = p - q
lower.reason: (D1) for f = +1 and -1, (LOC) and continuity hold on the whole diamond; the bound equals l1 C1 + l2 C2 + mu exactly
